subject.title: Feature request: message delete (revoke) action for WhatsApp channel

question: Should OpenClaw expose WhatsApp destructive message mutation now, and if so should the public action be delete, unsend, revoke, or an alias set with explicit safety semantics?
rationale: The source fix is bounded, but maintainer intent is required because the action mutates user-visible WhatsApp history, may affect sensitive data expectations, and has ambiguous provider semantics around the revoke window and local-only deletion.

options.title: Sponsor linked PR after safety proof
options.body: Settle the public action names, require own-message/fromMe and target-authorization enforcement plus live WhatsApp proof, then rebase/review the linked implementation or an equivalent replacement.

options.title: Keep open but pause implementation
options.body: Leave the feature request canonical while maintainers decide whether remote-revocation guarantees and user-facing error semantics are strong enough for agents.

options.title: Reject destructive WhatsApp mutation
options.body: Close this direction if maintainers decide the false-confidence or abuse risk outweighs the cleanup and incident-retraction value.

recommendation.title: Sponsor linked PR after safety proof
recommendation.body: Settle the public action names, require own-message/fromMe and target-authorization enforcement plus live WhatsApp proof, then rebase/review the linked implementation or an equivalent replacement.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete already provided maintainer review context on this issue and is the strongest visible decision signal for product/security acceptance.
